column1: # MODE: PROD
# Prebuilt binaries this skill SHIPS as artifacts, one row per target.
# This is a different budget from requires.tsv. requires.tsv declares what the
# target machine must already HAVE; this file declares what we DELIVER. A
# self-contained binary asks nothing of the box, so shipping one lowers the
# skill's runtime requirements rather than raising them — the python3/node/perl/
# socat any-of group in requires.tsv exists only because there is no binary yet.
# Rust is a DEV dependency: the toolchain builds these, and the source under
# src/ is MODE: DEV so it never ships. Users receive the compiled artifact and
# need no Rust, no cargo and no interpreter.
# Each binary lives at bin/<target>/<binary>. The installer matches `condition`
# against the host the same way requires.tsv rows are matched, and installs the
# first row that matches. Every binary ships in the npm package regardless of
# host, because we do not know who or what pulls it.
# Columns, tab-separated:
#   target     Rust target triple; also the directory name under bin/
#   condition  <uname -s glob>:<uname -m glob> this row serves, a bash case
#              pattern, so | may join alternatives (same grammar as
#              requires.tsv). The first matching row wins, top to bottom.
#   binary     filename inside bin/<target>/ — carries .exe on Windows
#   why        one line: which hosts this row serves, and why this triple
# Linux ships musl rather than gnu so one static binary covers every distro
# regardless of glibc version. magequery ships both because it links a C MySQL
# client; the chat server has no C dependencies, so musl alone is sufficient and
# one row per condition keeps selection unambiguous.
# Windows: one msvc build serves native Windows, Git Bash (MINGW*), MSYS2 and
# Cygwin, because all four report distinct `uname -s` values but run the same
# PE binary. rustc does list a tier-3 x86_64-pc-cygwin target, but tier 3 has
# no prebuilt std and no CI guarantee, and a Cygwin user is already served by
# the row below — so it is deliberately not shipped. Say the word if a native
# Cygwin build is wanted anyway; it costs a build-std step.
target
x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
column4: 64-bit x86 Linux; static musl so it runs on any distro and any glibc vintage, Alpine included

column1: aarch64-unknown-linux-musl
column4: 64-bit ARM Linux: Graviton, Ampere, Raspberry Pi 64-bit, arm64 devcontainers

column1: x86_64-apple-darwin
aarch64-apple-darwin
column4: Apple Silicon macOS; cross-built darwin-arm64 needs an ad-hoc signature or the kernel refuses to exec it

column1: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
column4: 64-bit Windows, and the POSIX layers on it: Git Bash, MSYS2 and Cygwin all run this PE binary
